title: Static and dynamic binding: who decides which method runs

videos.script: Every method call in Java is decided twice. This lesson is about who decides what, and when. {{types}} A variable of type Item holds a Book. The variable's type decides which methods you may call. The object decides which one runs. {{cast}} Ask an Item for its ISBN and the compiler refuses. Cast it to Book and the compiler agrees, and the JVM checks your word while the program runs. {{dispatch}} Then into the class file. The compiler wrote a call to Item's describe, and the JVM ran Book's. One instruction, three different methods. {{hidden}} Last, the things that do not work that way. Fields, static methods and private methods are fixed by the compiler, and a subclass cannot change them. A program prints parent where you expected child, and the bytecode shows why.
